cetiosaurus:enwiki:6.title: Cetiosaurus (The question of the type species)

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus fossils date to the Middle Jurassic period, specifically the Bajocian to Bathonian ages.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Middle Jurassic (Bajocian-Bathonian)~

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus lived approximately 171 to 165 million years ago in what is now Britain and possibly France.
facts.quote: living about 171 to 165 million years ago during the Bajocian and Bathonian ages in what is now Britain and probably France.

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus was named in 1842, becoming the first sauropod genus described from bones.
facts.quote: Cetiosaurus was named in 1842, making it the first sauropod from which bones were described

facts.statement: The genus name was chosen by Sir Richard Owen because he initially believed the animal was a large marine crocodile rather than a land-dwelling dinosaur.
facts.quote: It was so named because its describer, Sir Richard Owen, supposed it was a marine creature, initially an extremely large crocodile, and did not recognise it for a land-dwelling dinosaur.

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus oxoniensis was officially designated the type species of the genus in 2014.
facts.quote: C. oxoniensis was officially made the new type species in 2014.

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus was a quadrupedal herbivore with a long neck, small head, relatively long forelimbs, and a shorter tail compared to most sauropods.
facts.quote: Cetiosaurus was a quadrupedal, long-necked, small-headed herbivore. It had a shorter tail and neck than most sauropods. The forelimbs on the other hand, were relatively long.

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus is estimated to have reached a length of about 16 meters and a weight of roughly 11 tonnes.
facts.quote: It is estimated to have been about 16 m long and to have weighed roughly 11 t.

facts.statement: Sir Richard Owen named the genus Cetiosaurus in 1841, one year before he coined the term Dinosauria.
facts.quote: In 1841 biologist, comparative anatomist and palaeontologist Sir Richard Owen, named these as the genus Cetiosaurus, the year before he coined the term Dinosauria.

facts.statement: In 1842, Owen named two species, Cetiosaurus hypoolithicus and Cetiosaurus epioolithicus, based on their position relative to oolithic layers.
facts.quote: In 1842 Owen named two species in the genus: Cetiosaurus hypoolithicus and Cetiosaurus epioolithicus.

facts.statement: By 1849, it became clear that some fossils previously assigned to Cetiosaurus actually belonged to Iguanodontidae.
facts.quote: As became apparent in 1849, some of these bones were not sauropod in nature at all but of Iguanodontidae.

facts.statement: In 1842, Owen attributed a partial skeleton found near Blisworth, Northamptonshire, to Cetiosaurus medius, though the specimen was later lost.
facts.quote: In 1842, Owen noted a partial skeleton of a sauropod dinosaur consisting of "five vertebrae, a scapula, coracoid, sternal plate, and portions of limb bone", found in rock exposed by railway construction near Blisworth, Northamptonshire, which he attributed to the species Cetiosaurus medius.

facts.statement: A sauropod right femur was discovered near Bletchingdon in March 1868.
facts.quote: In March 1868, workers near Bletchingdon discovered a sauropod right femur.

facts.statement: Between March 1869 and June 1870, Professor John Phillips uncovered three skeletons and additional bone material at the Bletchingdon site.
facts.quote: Between March 1869 and June 1870 Professor John Phillips, further investigating the site, in a layer dating from the Bathonian uncovered three skeletons and additional bone material.

facts.statement: In 1871, John Phillips named C. oxoniensis and C. glymptonensis based on the Bletchingdon finds.
facts.quote: In 1871 based on these he named two species: Cetiosaurus oxoniensis (originally spelled Ceteosaurus Oxoniensis) and Cetiosaurus glymptonensis.

facts.statement: A specimen known as the 'Rutland Dinosaur' was unknowingly excavated on June 19, 1968, from a clay pit near Great Casterton, Rutland.
facts.quote: A century later, a new C. oxoniensis specimen (LCM G468.1968), subsequently named by the local media, the "Rutland Dinosaur", was unknowingly excavated on 19 June 1968 in the form of several tons of discarded siderite ironstone from a clay-pit near Great Casterton, Rutland

facts.statement: A provisional identification of the Rutland Dinosaur as C. oxoniensis was published in late 1970 by Michael Jones after corroboration by J.S. McIntosh.
facts.quote: It was not until late 1970 however that a provisional identification of C. oxoniensis was published by curator Michael Jones following examination and corroboration by Prof. J S McIntosh of the Peabody Museum of Natural History Yale University

facts.statement: The C. oxoniensis specimen at Leicester Museum and Art Gallery is 15 meters long and includes fourteen cervical, ten dorsal, five sacral, and about fifty caudal vertebrae.
facts.quote: The specimen on display at Leicester Museum and Art Gallery is 15 m (49 ft) in length and has fourteen cervical vertebrae, ten dorsals, five sacrals and about fifty caudals.

facts.statement: The name Cetiosaurus means 'whale lizard', derived from Greek words for 'sea monster' and 'lizard'.
facts.quote: Cetiosaurus ( meaning 'whale lizard', from the Greek /κήτειος meaning 'sea monster' (later, 'whale') and /σαυρος meaning 'lizard')

facts.statement: It is debated whether two tail vertebrae recorded by Lydekker in 1888 as originating from the Blisworth skeleton actually exist in the Natural History Museum collections, as they could not be located in a 2003 study.
facts.quote: It has been suggested that two tail vertebrae mentioned by Richard Lydekker in 1888 as being the collection of the Natural History Museum in London, which were catalogued as BMNH R16090 and R160901, and recorded as having been purchased from Blisworth by the museum in 1843, originate from the Blisworth skeleton. However in a 2003 paper on the taxonomy of Cetiosaurus, neither of the two vertebrae were able to be located in the museum's collections by the paper's authors.

facts.statement: In 1874, John Whitaker Hulke named Cetiosaurus humerocristatus based on a humerus found at Sandsfoot near Weymouth in Dorset.
facts.quote: In 1874, John Whitaker Hulke named Cetiosaurus humerocristatus, "with a crested humerus", based on specimen BMNH 44635, a humerus found that year at Sandsfoot near Weymouth in Dorset.

facts.statement: In 2010, Cetiosaurus humerocristatus was reclassified into the separate genus Duriatitan.
facts.quote: In 2010, this was made a separate genus Duriatitan.

facts.statement: Ornithopsis leedsii was named in 1887 by John Hulke based on fossils collected by Alfred Nicholson Leeds from the Oxford Clay.
facts.quote: Ornithopsis leedsii was named in 1887 by John Hulke for a pelvis, vertebrae and ribs collected by Alfred Nicholson Leeds, an English farmer and amateur fossil collector who throughout his life compiled numerous collections of fossils from the Oxford Clay.

facts.statement: Richard Lydekker suggested that Jurassic remains including O. leedsii and C. oxoniensis belonged to Cetiosaurus, while Wealden fossils belonged to Ornithopsis.
facts.quote: Lydekker suggested that Wealden fossils (including O. hulkei) belonged to Ornithopsis and the Jurassic remains (including O. leedsii and C. oxoniensis) to Cetiosaurus.

facts.statement: In 1927, Friedrich von Huene assigned C. leedsi to the separate genus Cetiosauriscus.
facts.quote: In 1927, Friedrich von Huene assigned C. leedsi to the separate genus Cetiosauriscus.

facts.statement: In 1970, Rodney Steel renamed Cardiodon Owen 1841 into Cetiosaurus rugulosus based on a lost tooth.
facts.quote: In 1970 Rodney Steel renamed Cardiodon Owen 1841, based on a now lost tooth, into Cetiosaurus rugulosus, "the wrinkled one".

facts.statement: In 2003, Upchurch and Martin rejected the identity of Cetiosaurus rugulosus.
facts.quote: In 2003, Upchurch & Martin rejected the identity.

facts.statement: In 1903, Sauvage concluded that Cetiosaurus rigauxi represented a pliosaurid.
facts.quote: In 1903, however, he was forced to conclude it represented a pliosaurid.

facts.statement: In 1880, Sauvage named the species Cetiosaurus philippsi.
facts.quote: In 1880, Sauvage named another species: Cetiosaurus philippsi.

facts.statement: In 1895, Lydekker referred the genus Ornithopsis to Atlantosauridae and assigned O. leedsii to the genus Pelorosaurus.
facts.quote: Lydekker in 1895 changed his mind and referred the species O. leedsii to Pelorosaurus (known already from the species P. brevis, once named Cetiosaurus brevis)—as P. leedsi—and referred the genus to Atlantosauridae.

facts.statement: In 1905, Arthur Smith Woodward placed C. leedsi in Cetiosaurus, including a partial sauropod skeleton from the Oxford Clay of Peterborough.
facts.quote: Arthur Smith Woodward supported Seeley's classification scheme in 1905, placing C. leedsi in Cetiosaurus, including within C. leedsi a partial sauropod skeleton collected from the Oxford Clay of Peterborough, England.

facts.statement: The holotype of C. leedsi is now considered indeterminate eusauropod remains (nomen dubium), while the Peterborough skeleton is assigned to the valid species Cetiosauriscus stewarti.
facts.quote: The holotype material of "C." leedsi, NHMUK R1988, consisting of a left and right ischium, is today considered indeterminate eusauropod remains, rendering the species a nomen dubium, while the sauropod skeleton described by Woodward from Peterborough in 1905 is now assigned to the valid separate species Cetiosauriscus stewarti.

facts.statement: Traditionally, C. medius was considered the type species of Cetiosaurus.
facts.quote: Traditionally, C. medius had been considered the type species of Cetiosaurus.

facts.statement: Of the four species named by Owen in 1842, only C. brevis was not a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: Of the four species named in Owen's second 1842 article, C. brevis, C. brachyurus, C. longus and C. medius, only C. brevis would not be a nomen dubium.

facts.statement: Upchurch and Martin suggested changing the type species to C. oxoniensis, the best-known species from the Middle Jurassic associated with the genus Cetiosaurus.
facts.quote: Therefore, Upchurch & Martin suggested to request the ICZN to change the type species into C. oxoniensis, the best known species from the Middle Jurassic, which the genus Cetiosaurus had generally come to be identified with.

facts.statement: In 2014, the ICZN officially made C. oxoniensis the type species of Cetiosaurus, replacing the original C. medius.
facts.quote: The ICZN accepted the proposal to change the type species in 2014 (Opinion 2331), officially making C. oxoniensis the type species in place of the original C. medius.

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus oxoniensis, named by Phillips in 1871, is the type species of Cetiosaurus.
facts.quote: The complex naming history can be summarised in a list of Cetiosaurus species: Cetiosaurus oxoniensis Phillips, 1871: type species of Cetiosaurus

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus hypoolithicus, named by Owen in 1841, is a nomen nudum.
facts.quote: Cetiosaurus hypoolithicus Owen, 1841: nomen nudum

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus epioolithicus, named by Owen in 1841, is a nomen nudum.
facts.quote: Cetiosaurus epioolithicus Owen, 1841: nomen nudum

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus brachyurus, named by Owen in 1842, is a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: Cetiosaurus brachyurus Owen, 1842: nomen dubium

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus longus, named by Owen in 1842, is a nomen dubium and is now considered Cetiosauriscus longus.
facts.quote: Cetiosaurus longus Owen, 1842: nomen dubium; = Cetiosauriscus longus (Owen, 1842) McIntosh, 1990

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus medius, named by Owen in 1842, is a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: Cetiosaurus medius Owen, 1842: nomen dubium

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus giganteus, cited by Huxley in 1870, is a nomen nudum.
facts.quote: Cetiosaurus giganteus Owen vide Huxley, 1870: nomen nudum

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus philippsi was named by Sauvage in 1880.
facts.quote: Cetiosaurus philippsi Sauvage, 1880

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus rigauxi is not a valid Cetiosaurus species and is identified as a pliosaurid.
facts.quote: Cetiosaurus rigauxi Sauvage, 1874: non Cetiosaurus, pliosaurid

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus leedsi is a nomen dubium and is equivalent to Ornithopsis leedsii.
facts.quote: Cetiosaurus leedsi (Hulke, 1887) Woodward, 1905: nomen dubium; = Ornithopsis leedsii Hulke, 1887

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus rugulosus is not a valid Cetiosaurus species and is now considered Cardiodon rugulosus.
facts.quote: Cetiosaurus rugulosus (Owen, 1845) Steel, 1970: non Cetiosaurus, = Cardiodon Owen, 1841; = Cardiodon rugulosus Owen, 1845

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus mogrebiensis is not a valid Cetiosaurus species.
facts.quote: Cetiosaurus mogrebiensis de Lapparent, 1955: non Cetiosaurus

facts.statement: Duriatitan humerocristatus is often considered a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: This today is often considered a nomen dubium.

facts.statement: If C. brevis were the type species, it would cause taxonomic instability because Pelorosaurus is recognized as a different kind of sauropod.
facts.quote: This conclusion, if correct, would cause considerable taxonomic instability, because the genus Pelorosaurus had since been based on its fossils, and recognized as a totally different kind of sauropod.

facts.statement: Upchurch and Martin suggested changing the type species to C. oxoniensis to stabilize the classification of Cetiosaurus.
facts.quote: Therefore, Upchurch & Martin suggested to request the ICZN to change the type species into C. oxoniensis, the best known species from the Middle Jurassic, which the genus Cetiosaurus had generally come to be identified with.

facts.statement: The fossils of Cetiosaurus include three skeletons discovered by Phillips.
facts.quote: These include the three skeletons found by Phillips.

facts.statement: A larger skeleton catalogued as OUMNH J13605–13613, J13615–16, J13619–J13688 and J13899 was selected by Upchurch & Martin as the lectotype.
facts.quote: One of these is a larger animal (catalogued as OUMNH J13605–13613, J13615–16, J13619–J13688 and J13899), which was chosen by Upchurch & Martin as the lectotype of the species

facts.statement: The Rutland specimen is about 40% complete and adds significantly to the known skeletal elements, particularly in the neck.
facts.quote: The Rutland specimen, about 40% complete, increases considerably the number of known skeletal elements, especially in the neck.

facts.statement: The skull is largely unknown, except possibly for the brain case found in specimen OUMNH J13596.
facts.quote: The skull is largely unknown, perhaps with the exception of the brain case represented by specimen OUMNH J13596.

facts.statement: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated the body length at 16 meters and body mass at 11 tonnes.
facts.quote: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated the body length at 16 m and body mass at 11 t.

facts.statement: The thigh bone was approximately six feet long.
facts.quote: Its thigh bone was approximately six feet long.

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus was the first sauropod whose bones were described in 1842.
facts.quote: Cetiosaurus fue en 1842 el primer saurópodo del que se describieron los huesos

facts.statement: C. oxoniensis is based on three more or less complete specimens discovered from 1868 onwards.
facts.quote: C. oxoniensis se basa en tres especímenes más o menos completos, descubiertos a partir de 1868 en adelante.

facts.statement: C. oxoniensis was a primitive herbivore, quadruped with a long neck and small head.
facts.quote: C. oxoniensis era un herbívoro "primitivo", cuadrúpedo , de cuello largo y cabeza pequeña .

facts.statement: C. oxoniensis is estimated to have been about 16 meters long and weighed approximately 11 tonnes.
facts.quote: Se estima que C. oxoniensis tenía unos 16 metros de largo y pesaba aproximadamente 11 toneladas.

facts.statement: The fossil range of Cetiosaurus is the Middle Jurassic.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Jurásico Medio

facts.statement: They lived in the middle Jurassic, between 171 and 169 million years ago, during the Bajocian and Bathonian stages.
facts.quote: vivieron a mediados del período Jurásico , hace entre 171 a 169 millones de años, entre el Bajociense y el Bathoniense

facts.statement: They lived in what is now Europe and Africa.
facts.quote: en lo que es hoy Europa y África.

facts.statement: The genus authority is Owen, 1841.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Owen, 1841

facts.statement: The type species is Cetiosaurus oxoniensis.
facts.quote: type_species: Cetiosaurus oxoniensis

facts.statement: The authority for the type species is Phillips, 1871.
facts.quote: type_species_authority: Phillips, 1871

facts.statement: The family is Cetiosauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Cetiosauridae

facts.statement: In 1869, Thomas Huxley explicitly stated that Cetiosaurus was a dinosaur.
facts.quote: In 1869 Thomas Huxley stated explicitly that Cetiosaurus was a dinosaur.

facts.statement: In 1888, Lydekker assigned Cetiosaurus to its own family, the Cetiosauridae.
facts.quote: In 1888 Lydekker assigned Cetiosaurus to its own family: the Cetiosauridae.

facts.statement: Paul considered Cetiosaurus a feeding generalist that ate at both low and medium-high levels due to its moderately long neck and limb proportions.
facts.quote: Paul considered Cetiosaurus a feeding generalist, eating at both a low and a medium-high level, in view of its moderately long neck and limb proportions.

facts.statement: The environment where Cetiosaurus lived consisted of floodplains and open woodlands.
facts.quote: The environment in which Cetiosaurus lived was floodplain and open woodland.

facts.statement: In their 2003 revision, Upchurch & Martin identified five autapomorphies of C. oxoniensis.
facts.quote: In their 2003 revision of the genus, Upchurch & Martin identified five autapomorphies of C. oxoniensis.

facts.statement: The lower process of the ilium features a triangular depression on the outer surface of its base.
facts.quote: The lower process of the ilium, to which the pubic bone was attached, features on the outer surface of its base a triangular depression.

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus was a primitive quadrupedal long-necked herbivore that reached 18 meters in length.
facts.quote: Cetiosaurus fue un primitivo herbívoro cuadrúpedo de cuello largo que alcanzó los 18 metros de largo

facts.statement: Its neck was about as long as its body, and its tail was considerably longer, consisting of at least 40 caudal vertebrae.
facts.quote: Su cuello era del mismo largo que su cuerpo, y la cola era considerablemente más larga, consistiendo en por lo menos 40 vértebras caudales

facts.statement: Its dorsal vertebrae were heavy and primitive, differing from the hollow bones of advanced sauropods like Brachiosaurus.
facts.quote: Sus vértebras dorsales, los huesos a lo largo de la espalda, eran pesadas y primitivas, diferentes de los huesos ahuecados de los saurópodos avanzados como Brachiosaurus

facts.statement: Its ulna was nearly as long as its humerus, unlike most other sauropods.
facts.quote: Su ulna, era casi tan larga como el húmero, a diferencia de la mayoría de los otros saurópodos

facts.statement: Its femur was approximately 1.2 meters in length.
facts.quote: Su fémur era aproximadamente 1,2 metros de longitud

facts.statement: Paul considered Cetiosaurus a feeding generalist that ate at low to medium-high levels, based on its moderately long neck and limb proportions.
facts.quote: Paul consideró Cetiosaurus un generalista de alimentación, comiendo a un nivel bajo y medio alto, en vista de sus proporciones moderadamente largas de cuello y extremidades

facts.statement: It shared its territory with predators like Megalosaurus and Eustreptospondylus in an environment of floodplains and open woodlands.
facts.quote: Compartió el territorio con predadores con el Megalosaurus y Eustreptospondylus en un ambiente de llanura inundable y bosques abiertos

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus, or specifically the neotype species C. oxoniensis, is known from relatively complete fossils.
facts.quote: Cetiosaurus , o específicamente la especie neotipo C. oxoniensis, es conocida a partir de fósiles relativamente completos

facts.statement: The known fossils include three skeletons found by Phillips.
facts.quote: Estos incluyen los tres esqueletos encontrados por Phillips

facts.statement: The largest skeleton, cataloged with multiple numbers, was chosen by Upchurch and Martin as the lectotype of the species.
facts.quote: Uno de estos es el más grande catalogado como OUMNH J13605-13613, J13615-16, J13619-J13688 y J13899 que fue elegido por Upchurch & Martin como el lectotipo de la especie

facts.statement: The Rutland sample, approximately 40% complete, significantly increases the number of known skeletal elements, especially in the neck.
facts.quote: La muestra de Rutland, esta aproximadamente 40% completa, aumenta considerablemente el número de elementos esqueléticos conocidos, especialmente en el cuello

facts.statement: The skull is largely unknown, perhaps except for the base of the skull represented by specimen OUMNH J13596.
facts.quote: El cráneo es en gran parte desconocido, quizás con la excepción del caso de la base del cráneo representado por el espécimen OUMNH J13596

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus was the first sauropod discovered.
facts.quote: Cetiosaurus fue el primer saurópodo descubierto

facts.statement: The first fossils found consisted of a vertebra, rib, and arm bone discovered on the Isle of Wight, England.
facts.quote: Los primeros fósiles encontrados consisten en una vértebra, costilla y el hueso del brazo descubiertos en isla del Wight Inglaterra

facts.statement: In the 1830s, before it was named, expert George Cuvier identified those fossils as whale bones.
facts.quote: En la década de 1830s, antes de que se nombrara, el experto George Cuvier identificó esos fósiles como huesos de ballena

facts.statement: In 1841, after discovering two more specimens, Richard Owen suggested naming this specimen Cetiosaurus because it resembled a 'whale reptile' in some sense.
facts.quote: En 1841, tras haber descubierto 2 ejemplares más, Richard Owen sugirió llamar a este espécimen Cetiosaurus, ya que en cierto sentido se asemejaba mucho a un "reptil ballena"

facts.statement: Its true nature was not observed until Thomas Huxley named it a dinosaur in 1869.
facts.quote: La naturaleza verdadera no fue observada hasta que Thomas Huxley lo nombrara como un dinosaurio en 1869

facts.statement: In 1979, a Cetiosaurus femur was found in Morocco that was nearly as high as a soccer goal.
facts.quote: En 1979 se encontró el fémur de un cetiosaurio en Marruecos que era casi tan alto como una portería de fútbol

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus oxoniensis lived in the Middle Jurassic of Oxfordshire and Rutland.
facts.quote: Cetiosaurus oxoniensis, del Jurásico Medio de Oxfordshire y Rutland

facts.statement: Its parent group is Gravisauria.
facts.quote: Parent group: Gravisauria

facts.statement: It is classified in the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: Its time range is from the Aalenian to the Aptian, between 174.7 and 119.57 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aalenian to Aptian (174.7 to 119.57 million years ago)

facts.statement: The material of C. medius is insufficient to include it in Cetiosaurus, so it is considered a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: El material de C. medius es insuficiente para incluirlo en Cetiosaurus por lo que se lo considera nomen dubium

facts.statement: Now that such relatives have been found, the uniqueness of C. oxoniensis and its status as a valid taxon must be proven by indicating its new derived traits or autapomorphies.
facts.quote: Ahora que se han encontrado tales parientes, la singularidad de C. oxoniensis y su estado como un taxón válido deben probarse indicando sus nuevos rasgos derivados o autapomorfias
